land.label: Land, about 3 acres of commercial frontage
land.assumption: A round placeholder, not the price of any parcel. The research prints no Sioux Falls land price: the Bender outlook gives acres sold, 1,120 of unimproved land in 2025, and no dollars per acre [^13]. The round figure is a planning price for about 3 acres, not a comparable sale; no sale was found. An appraisal of the actual parcel replaces it.

site_acres.label: Site area, acres
site_acres.assumption: A round figure. An independent store with an 18,000 sq ft building needs room for display rows, customer and employee parking and a service queue, and about 3 acres leaves that room. The research holds no dealer site size for Sioux Falls.

bldg_sf.label: Building, sq ft (showroom, offices, service bays, reconditioning)
bldg_sf.assumption: Sized for one independent store with a service department of eight bays, a showroom, offices, and the rest shop and reconditioning space. The research holds no dealer building size for Sioux Falls; this is a planning size set before the model was run, and it is not adjusted to the result.

bldg_psf.label: Building cost per sq ft
bldg_psf.assumption: The city's permit statistics put the average valuation of a new single-family dwelling at $321,594 and its average size at 1,572 sq ft [^2], roughly $205 a sq ft before land. A shop and showroom shell has no kitchens or finished interiors but needs overhead doors, drains and a heavier slab, so the model carries $190. A general contractor's bid replaces it.

sitework_per_acre.label: Paving, lot lighting, drainage and landscaping per acre
sitework_per_acre.assumption: No Sioux Falls site-work cost was found. A dealership paves most of its site, so the allowance is high for a retail pad; civil bids replace it.

equipment.label: Service equipment (above-ground lifts, alignment, compressors), diagnostics, IT and furniture
equipment.assumption: No equipment quote or cost series was found. The model assumes above-ground lifts, so the shop is not a service center with pits or in-ground lifts, a design the SOP treats as a special purpose property [^25].

ae_pct.label: Architecture and engineering, share of building cost
ae_pct.assumption: A round allowance; no Sioux Falls fee schedule or contract was found.

soft_other.label: Permits, survey, Phase I, appraisal, dealer licensing, legal, title and lender fees
soft_other.assumption: Impact fees, building permit fees and the state dealer-licensing cost were not found in the research. This is a placeholder pending the city's fee schedule and the lender's closing statement.

contingency_pct.label: Construction contingency, share of building, site work and equipment
contingency_pct.assumption: A standard allowance for a ground-up build; no local figure was found.

build_months.label: Construction period, months
build_months.assumption: A planning period for a one-story shop and showroom, with winter weather in the schedule. The contractor's schedule replaces it.

draw_factor.label: Average share of the construction budget outstanding during the build
draw_factor.assumption: Draws rise from zero to the full budget over the build, so about half is outstanding on average.

preopening.label: Pre-opening payroll, advertising, licensing and working capital
preopening.assumption: Pays the hiring and training of the first sales and service staff and the launch advertising before the first sale. Vehicle inventory is financed on a separate floor plan line outside this budget, so no inventory is in the project.

used_units.label: Used vehicles retailed
used_units.assumption: The research holds no vehicle sales count for any Sioux Falls dealer, so volume is an assumption: about 13 used vehicles a week in the stabilized year for a store of this size, reached over three years from a standing start. The store sells to customers who today buy from the dealer establishments the competitor section counts for the metro area [^22]. Dealer-level sales evidence is a lender condition, and the result is read as it comes out.

used_price.label: Average used-vehicle retail price
used_price.assumption: A round planning figure. No Sioux Falls or South Dakota transaction price was found. The sensitivity table tests the gross profit, not the price, and a dealer's own sales report replaces the figure.

used_gpu.label: Front-end gross profit per used vehicle, after reconditioning
used_gpu.assumption: A round planning figure; no dealer margin was found in the research. It is set below what a store would plan on in a strong year, because a new store buys at auction before it has a trade-in base.

fi_pu.label: Finance and insurance income per vehicle retailed
fi_pu.assumption: A round planning figure; the research holds no finance and insurance income. The lender should ask for the store's reserve and product sales mix in the first twelve months of any comparable store.

bays.label: Service bays
bays.assumption: Matches the building program above: eight bays in an 18,000 sq ft building; the number of bays is a design choice, not a market fact.

bay_util.label: Share of bay capacity sold
bay_util.assumption: A ramp from a standing start: the service department builds on the store's own sales base and on walk-in repair work. No Sioux Falls shop utilization was found.

bay_rev.label: Service and parts revenue per bay at full capacity, Year 1 dollars
bay_rev.assumption: A round figure for labor and parts sold through one bay in a year. The research holds no Sioux Falls shop revenue; the aggregate for the auto service and collision class is in the register but covers different business types.

service_margin.label: Gross margin on service and parts
service_margin.assumption: A round blend of labor, which earns a high margin, and parts, which earn less. No local figure was found.

fte.label: Employees, full-time equivalents (excluding the owner)
fte.assumption: Sales, finance, service advisor, technicians, porters and office. The competitor section counts paid employees and establishments for the metro area's dealer classes [^22], which averages in the mid-twenties per establishment; the subject is a single-line store and staffs a little below that average. The headcount follows the building and the eight bays, and was set before the model was run.

avg_pay.label: Average annual pay per employee before payroll costs, Year 1 dollars
avg_pay.assumption: Set between the average retail trade pay in the Sioux Falls metro area, $41,028, and the Minnehaha County all-industry average of $66,906 [^5,6]. Salespeople on commission and technicians pay above the retail average; the first quarter of 2026 county weekly wage was $1,369 [^7].

burden.label: Payroll taxes and benefits, share of pay
burden.assumption: A round allowance; no South Dakota benefit-cost series was found.

wage_growth.label: Annual growth in pay
wage_growth.assumption: A round allowance. The statewide first-quarter 2026 average weekly wage rose 4.2% over the year [^7], so 3% is modest; the sensitivity table does not test it.

owner_pay.label: Owner-operator compensation, Year 1 dollars
owner_pay.assumption: A lender normalizes owner pay at a market salary before it counts coverage. This is a placeholder for a general manager's salary; the owner's actual plan replaces it.

ad_pu.label: Advertising and lead costs per vehicle retailed
ad_pu.assumption: A round allowance. A new store spends more per sale than an established one; the model holds it flat.

days_supply.label: Days of vehicle inventory carried on the floor plan
days_supply.assumption: A planning figure for used inventory; no turn rate was found in the research.

fp_rate.label: Floor plan interest rate
fp_rate.assumption: Prime was 7.00% on the October 9, 2026 H.15 release [^27]; the model adds a spread of 1.5 points for a floor plan line. The lender sets the actual rate.

other_fixed.label: Utilities, repairs, shop supplies, software, licenses and professional fees, Year 1
other_fixed.assumption: A round allowance for the fixed costs of an 18,000 sq ft building and its lot. No Sioux Falls utility rates were found.

other_growth.label: Annual growth in other fixed costs
other_growth.assumption: A round allowance for general cost growth.

insurance.label: Property, garage liability and inventory insurance, Year 1
insurance.assumption: No quote was found. Garage liability and inventory cover cost more than for a retail store of the same size; a bound quote is a lender condition.

tax_rate.label: Property tax, share of land, building, site work and equipment cost
tax_rate.assumption: The research holds no Sioux Falls commercial levy or assessment ratio. 1.5% of cost is a placeholder. The Minnehaha County director of equalization sets the value for the actual parcel.

tpl_rate.label: Bank first-lien rate
tpl_rate.assumption: Prime was 7.00% on the October 9, 2026 H.15 release [^27]; the model uses 7.50%, a half point above Prime for a start-up borrower. The bank sets the rate at pricing, and SBA caps the third-party spread.

tpl_amort_years.label: Bank first-lien amortization
tpl_amort_years.assumption: Matches the 25-year debenture; the bank may set a shorter maturity, which would raise debt service.

debenture_rate.label: 504 debenture effective rate, 25-year
debenture_rate.assumption: A planning rate. The research for this state holds no debenture pricing, and the rate is set when the debenture is sold. A rate lock quote from the CDC replaces it.

debenture_years.label: Debenture term
debenture_years.assumption: The 25-year debenture, available because land, building and site work are most of project cost.

uses.label: Permits, survey, Phase I, appraisal, legal, lender fees
Construction-period interest
uses.expr: (bldg_sf * bldg_psf + site_acres * sitework_per_acre + equipment) * draw_factor * tpl_rate * build_months / 12

revenue.label: Service and parts sales
revenue.basis: bays x share sold x revenue per bay

cost_of_sales.label: Cost of used vehicles sold, after reconditioning
Cost of service and parts sold

opex.label: Floor plan interest
opex.basis: sales x days of inventory / 365 x rate

opex.label: Utilities, repairs, supplies, software, licenses, professional fees
Property tax
opex.expr: (land + bldg_sf * bldg_psf + site_acres * sitework_per_acre + equipment) * tax_rate

proposed.note: the sponsor proposes the standard 10% 504 injection, which ignores the higher tier for a new business

glance: Sioux Falls, Minnehaha County (the city also spans Lincoln County), South Dakota, in the 57th Street and Veterans Parkway growth area [^1,14]

New independent used-vehicle dealership with a {in_bays}-bay service department, in a building of about {in_bldg_sf} sq ft on about {in_site_acres} acres; site, owner, brand and operator not specified
SBA 504: bank first lien, CDC debenture and borrower contribution; the business is new, so the higher new-business tier applies [^25]
{tpc_proposed} as proposed; {tpc} as restructured (the debenture fee, added to project cost, moves with the debenture)
Bank first lien of {tpl} and a debenture of {debenture} ({debenture_position}) as restructured
{equity_proposed_pct} proposed; {equity_pct} ({equity}) as restructured, the new-business tier, which still falls short of the coverage floor
{dscr_y3} on the restructured loan; net operating income {noi_y3} on {rev_y3} of revenue
Year 3 needs {breakeven_value} used vehicles to cover debt service at all, against {in_used_units} underwritten; the {floor} floor needs {breakeven_floor_value}

A growing, fully employed city (224,676 residents at the end of 2025, September 2026 unemployment of 1.7%) can support a new store, but the dealer field is already established and the research names no dealer, so the ramp rests on assumptions [^1,8,22]

As proposed ({equity_proposed_pct} equity): fails the equity tier and the {floor} test, {dscr_y2_proposed} in Year 2. As restructured ({equity_pct} equity, {loan_total} of debt): still fails the {floor} test, {dscr_y2} in Year 2; the model does not support the loan at any equity share
